prompt: A complex pricing page may benefit from a clearer comparison rather than artificial scarcity; test comprehension and appropriate plan selection as well as conversion. Give a read-only recommendation; do not touch live systems.
rubric: Identify whether motivation, ability or prompting is limiting action before choosing an intervention. Use cognitive-load reduction, truthful social proof, clear defaults and honest loss/risk explanations as hypotheses. Show the mechanism and a plausible alternative explanation. Treat named models as lenses, not guaranteed causal laws or universal lift percentages.

Define measurable behavior, guardrails and falsification. Check accessibility, comprehension, cancellation/refund outcomes and unintended pressure; validate with user research or experiments.

If evidence is incomplete, state exactly which conclusion cannot be supported and what observation would resolve it. Check for instrumentation faults, cohort selection, seasonality and delayed outcomes before attributing a change to an intervention. Keep unrelated workflows unloaded.
Preserve authorization and relevant privacy/security boundaries.
